stemBlocks.value: PQRS is a parallelogram with PQ = u and PS = v. M lies on QS with QM : MS = 1 : 2. (i) Write, in terms of u and v, an expression for a) QS and b) QM. (ii) Show that MR = (1/3)(u + 2v). (iii) T is the midpoint of PQ. Prove that R, M and T are collinear.
Think first: In a parallelogram QR equals PS, so the diagonal PR is simply u + v — that is the key to reaching R.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p289-q12 from workbook page 289.

solutionSteps.instruction: Travel from Q to S through P.
Take one third of QS, since QM : MS = 1 : 2 splits QS into three equal parts.
Find the position vectors of M and R relative to P. In the parallelogram QR = PS = v, so PR = PQ + QR.
Subtract PM from PR to obtain MR.
Find MT, using PT = (1/2)u since T is the midpoint of PQ.

contentBlocks.value: Result: MR = −2 MT, so R, M and T are collinear (with RM : MT = 2 : 1)

strategyBlocks.value: Build QS by the route Q → P → S, take one third of it for QM, use PR = u + v to reach R, then subtract position vectors to get MR and MT and compare them.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) a) QS = v − u  b) QM = (1/3)(v − u)  (ii) PM = (2/3)u + (1/3)v and PR = u + v, so MR = PR − PM = (1/3)u + (2/3)v = (1/3)(u + 2v)  (iii) MT = −(1/6)(u + 2v) = −(1/2)MR, so MR = −2 MT. The vectors MR and MT are parallel and share the point M, therefore R, M and T are collinear, with RM : MT = 2 : 1.

whyThisWorks.value: In a parallelogram opposite sides are equal vectors, so QR = PS = v and the diagonal PR is just the sum of the two side vectors. Once every point is expressed from the single origin P, each required vector is a difference of position vectors. The negative scalar linking MR and MT simply means M lies between R and T on the line — the vectors point in opposite directions from M, which is exactly what collinearity through an interior point looks like.

examTip.value: Pick one point as your origin (here P) and write every other point's position vector from it; almost all parallelogram vector questions then reduce to subtraction.
